input.quote: Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights or obligations hereunder, whether by operation of law or otherwise, without the prior written consent of the other party. Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party shall have the right to assign this Agreement in connection with the merger or acquisition of such party or the sale of all or substantially all of its assets related to this Agreement without such consent, except in the case where such transaction involves a direct competitor of the other party where consent of the other party will be required.
input.rationale: Section 14.1 is a symmetric bar on assignment: it gives us no affiliate carve-out, applies no reasonableness standard to consent, and its competitor carve-back lets Commerce One block our merger/acquisition or asset-sale assignment if the acquirer is its competitor — leverage over our corporate transactions that the playbook treats as unacceptable. Section 11 contains no change-of-control termination or re-pricing right, so only the assignment clause needs fixing. The redline gives us affiliate and successor assignment rights without consent and confines the consent requirement and competitor prohibition to Commerce One, per the preferred position.

proposal.summary: Give Corio affiliate/successor assignment rights without consent and limit Commerce One's assignment to consented, non-competitor transfers
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We revised the assignment clause so we may assign freely to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets, without the competitor carve-back that would let Commerce One block our corporate transactions, and so Commerce One may assign only with our consent (not unreasonably withheld) and never to our competitor. This reflects our standard position that a vendor should not gain leverage over our M&A activity; if helpful, we can accept a mutual notice-based successor right with consent not unreasonably withheld for other assignments.

Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party shall have the right to assign this Agreement in connection with the merger or acquisition of such party or the sale of all or substantially all of its assets related to this Agreement without such consent, except in the case where such transaction involves a direct competitor of the other party where consent of the other party will be required.
ops.newText: Commerce One may not assign this Agreement or any rights or obligations hereunder, whether by operation of law or otherwise, without the prior written consent of Corio (which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld), and in no event may Commerce One assign this Agreement to a direct competitor of Corio. Corio may assign this Agreement, in whole or in part, without the consent of Commerce One to an affiliate of Corio or to a successor in connection with the merger or acquisition of Corio or the sale of all or substantially all of its assets related to this Agreement.
